title: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN lacks D1:Edit, blocking migrations in CI
description: First real migration run (run 31210455090) failed: 'A request to the Cloudflare API (/accounts/***/d1/database/ff3a01c8-aedb-4bc2-8231-b8511b353728/query) failed. title: apps/api dev server has no D1 binding or vars, so local signup 500s
description:
cd apps/api && pnpm dev starts a Worker that cannot serve any authenticated route. POST /auth/signup returns 500 with {"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')"} - reproduced directly with curl against the running worker.

Cause: the dev script is plain `wrangler dev` with no --env, so wrangler loads wrangler.toml's TOP-LEVEL block. That block has name, main, compatibility_date, compatibility_flags and routes - and no d1_databases and no [vars]. The code reads env.DB in 11 places and env.JWT_SECRET in 5, so both are undefined. .prepare() throws on the first database call, which is why the error surfaces as a D1 symptom rather than a config one.

Two separate misses, so fixing only the binding leaves you with a second failure on JWT_SECRET:
  - [[env.development.d1_databases]] exists in wrangler.toml but is commented out
  - [env.development.vars] is defined but never loaded, because dev does not pass --env development

DEV.md documents local setup as just `pnpm dev` and never mentions a database step. Its own checklist still has 'User CRUD operations (D1 queries)' unticked, which suggests local signup has never worked rather than having regressed.

Worked around for now by setting VITE_USE_MOCK_API=true in apps/web/.env.development, which serves the whole auth surface from src/api/mockApi.ts with no backend.
acceptance_criteria: cd apps/api && pnpm dev, then POST /auth/signup succeeds against a local D1 with packages/db's migrations applied. DEV.md documents whatever setup step that needs. apps/web can set VITE_USE_MOCK_API=false and sign up for real.
notes: The dev vars also still describe a Postgres setup (DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME) that no code reads - leftover from before D1. Worth removing while in there so the config stops describing an architecture the app does not have.
close_reason: Fixed. pnpm dev now passes --env development, the development d1_databases binding is uncommented (onlooker-db-local, fake all-zero database_id since wrangler dev is local-first, migrations_dir pointing at packages/db), and DEV.md documents the migrations step plus the exact 500 you get without it. Also made WorkerEnv.DB required and removed the ten env.DB! assertions that were letting a missing binding reach runtime, and dropped the dead DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_NAME Postgres vars from both the config and the type. Verified live: signup 201, login 200, wrong password 401, duplicate signup 409.

title: Two repos deploy a worker named onlooker-community-website
description:
Both this monorepo's apps/website and the org's separate onlooker-community/website repo declare a Cloudflare worker named onlooker-community-website. Same name, same account, so whichever deploys last wins and silently replaces the other.

apps/website is the intended owner — it is the actively developed plugin catalog and now serves onlooker.dev. The separate repo is legacy: last pushed 2026-06-27, and its site was a single landing page.

The saving grace today is that the legacy repo has no CI at all — no .github/workflows directory — so it cannot republish automatically. The risk is a person running wrangler deploy from a local checkout, which would overwrite the live marketing site with six-week-old code and produce no failure anywhere.

Now that CI deploys apps/website on every merge, the collision is live in both directions.
acceptance_criteria: The legacy onlooker-community/website repository is archived, so deploying from it requires deliberately unarchiving first. Confirm by checking the repo shows as archived and that a fresh merge to onlooker main still leaves onlooker.dev serving the monorepo's site.
notes: Found 2026-08-12 while investigating why the brand rebuild merged but never appeared on onlooker.dev. Archiving is a GitHub action the user takes; nothing to change in this repo. Filed at P1 because the failure mode is silent and hits the public marketing domain.
close_reason: The onlooker-community/website repo is archived (verified via the API), so deploying from it now requires deliberately unarchiving first. apps/website in this monorepo is the sole owner of the onlooker-community-website worker. Confirmed onlooker.dev still serves the monorepo's build after archiving.

title: Verify the heartbeat once it is registered on main
description: The heartbeat workflow could not be exercised before merge: GitHub only registers a workflow once it exists on the default branch, and --ref selects among already-registered workflows rather than registering a new one. So the workflow itself shipped unverified by design, and this is the verification it is owed. The script underneath was verified live against both environments including its failure paths; only the Actions glue is untested.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 'gh workflow run Heartbeat' completes successfully. 2) Its log shows all six check lines - three per environment. A green run alone is NOT sufficient: if the script were never reached the job would also be green. 3) Roughly ten minutes after a run, Cloudflare's request-by-hostname chart shows a non-zero floor for all four hosts. If it does not, stop and report rather than continuing - either analytics lag (wait and re-check) or the requests never reach the analytics pipeline, and the second would invalidate the design rather than the implementation.
notes:
MEASURED CADENCE 2026-08-09: GitHub delivers the '*/5' cron at ~31 min, not 5. Three consecutive scheduled runs at 19:23, 19:54, 20:25 — gaps of 31/31/31 min. Consistent enough to be a throttle rather than jitter, though the sample is only ~1.5 h.

Revised expected volumes (previous figures in this bead and in the spec assumed 5 min and are WRONG by ~6x):
  runs/day            ~46   (not 288)
  api-production       ~93 invocations/day  (not 576)
  web-production       ~46/day              (not 288)
  total requests       ~277/day             (not 1728)

Consequences: (1) do not set dashboard thresholds on the 5-min figures; (2) charts bucketed at 5 min show mostly-empty buckets with sparse spikes rather than a continuous floor — bucket hourly or wider; (3) outage detection latency is ~31-62 min, not 5-10; (4) ~277 req/day is thin for Cloudflare's sampled datasets, so low-count charts stay imprecise.

The design's core purpose still holds — a flatline is still detectable — but at 31-min resolution.

title: Test runner's compatibility date was unpinned, breaking CI at midnight
description: apps/api/vitest.config.ts set no compatibilityDate, so vitest-pool-workers asked workerd for today's date. workerd 1.20260801.1 supports up to 2026-08-08, so at midnight on 2026-08-09 every run started failing with ERR_RUNTIME_FAILURE and 'no tests' - locally and in CI, on every PR and merge, with no code change involved. Fixed by pinning compatibilityDate to 2024-12-16 to match apps/api/wrangler.toml, which also makes the tests run under the same compatibility date as the deployed worker instead of a newer one. Worth knowing the failure mode: the suite reported 'no tests' rather than a failure, so a careless reading looks like a pass.
close_reason: Fixed in the same change that found it: compatibilityDate pinned to 2024-12-16 in apps/api/vitest.config.ts. Verified - api suite back to 14/14 and the workspace to 13/13.

title: Execute the D1 rebuild runbook to reconcile production with the schema
description: docs/runbooks/2026-08-08-database-rebuild.md is written, reviewed twice, and ready, but has NOT been run. Until it is, production still has the drifted schema (first_name/last_name plus an ALTER-appended name, sessions.token_hash without UNIQUE or CASCADE, an undeclared audit_logs table) while the code on main expects the new one. Human-executed only: it drops production tables. Order matters - the drop must precede the merge, because the new migration uses bare CREATE TABLE and will error against still-present tables. Blocks closing onlooker-1g9.
close_reason: Rebuild executed 2026-08-09. Both D1 databases dropped and rebuilt from the drizzle baseline; d1_migrations cleared so the false ledger is discarded rather than built upon. Verified by direct query, not by log: production users.email_verified is now text (was BOOLEAN), first_name/last_name gone, sessions.token_hash carries its UNIQUE index and the FK cascades, audit_logs and its five undeclared indexes removed, 9 indexes matching the generated migration, and d1_migrations records exactly 0000_kind_starjammers.sql. The CI schema verifier ran between migrate and deploy in both environments, so neither worker shipped against an unverified schema. Real signup/login round-trips pass on both api-staging and api, and the persisted row shows email_verified as a genuine null with a 64-char token hash. test@onlooker.dev was dropped deliberately - it was disposable test data with all name fields null, which also removed the boolean-to-timestamp remapping entirely.

title: Automate deploys: run D1 migrations, deploy staging from main, gate prod
description: Make deploys self-sufficient. (1) Apply D1 migrations as a deploy step - both databases currently have zero tables (onlooker-8sn), so the API deploys green but cannot serve any DB-backed route. Use apps/api/migrations as the source of truth since apps/api/src/db/queries.ts hand-writes SQL against it (token_hash on sessions); packages/db drizzle schema has drifted and is not a dependency of apps/api. (2) Deploy staging automatically on push to main - no staging branch exists so deploy-staging has never run. (3) Production stays behind the existing GitHub environment approval gate and additionally requires staging to have succeeded. (4) Give api-staging.onlooker.dev a custom_domain so Cloudflare provisions the missing DNS record itself.
design: Chose apps/api/migrations over packages/db drizzle schema because it matches the deployed code. Staging triggers from main rather than a staging branch to avoid maintaining a second long-lived branch. Production routing left as-is on plain routes because it is live and working - only staging converts to custom_domain.
close_reason: Closed

title: Staging D1 schema is stale and predates the current API
description: CORRECTION: the original premise was wrong. Cloudflare's d1_databases_list reports num_tables=0 for both databases, but that metadata is stale - direct queries show both are populated. Production (5473b131) holds 1 user and 2 sessions and its schema MATCHES the deployed API: sessions.token_hash and users.name both present, verification_tokens exact. Production auth works; the earlier claim that it could not is retracted. The real fault is staging (ff3a01c8), which carries an older schema from a different era: sessions has token/refresh_token/refresh_expires_at and NO token_hash, users has first_name/last_name and no name, plus a stray audit_logs table from the drizzle schema. That is why 0001_init.sql fails at line 52, CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_token_hash ON sessions(token_hash) - the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS above it is a no-op against the pre-existing table. Staging holds ZERO rows in every table, so dropping and rebuilding is lossless. d1_migrations is empty in staging and absent entirely in production, so these tables were never created through the migration system.
notes: Migration verified safe against production: all three CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS are no-ops, and every one of the 9 indexes targets a column production already has. Applying it there would only record 0001_init as applied.
close_reason: Resolved end-to-end in run 31210455090 attempt 3. Token gained D1:Edit; stale staging tables (0 rows) dropped and rebuilt by the migration. Staging now has users/sessions/verification_tokens plus all 9 indexes, and the real queries.ts session lookup runs against it. Production migrated cleanly with its 1 user and 2 sessions intact and d1_migrations now recording 0001_init.sql. All four endpoints return 200, including api-staging.onlooker.dev which never resolved before.

title: CI deploy jobs invoke pnpm builtin deploy instead of wrangler
description: Deploy steps run 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/api deploy --env production'. 'deploy' is a pnpm BUILTIN command (deploys a workspace package to a directory), so it shadows the package script and pnpm rejects --env: [ERROR] Unknown option: 'env'. This is why the post-merge push run on main fails at Deploy to Production even though quality and test now pass. Compounding it, apps/web has no deploy script at all, so even 'pnpm run deploy' would fail there. Root package.json already defines the correct form: deploy:api:prod = 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/api exec wrangler deploy --env production'. Verified both api and web with 'wrangler deploy --env production --dry-run'.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/deploy-wrangler-invocation: deploy steps now call the root deploy:api:prod / deploy:web:prod scripts, which use 'exec wrangler deploy --env <env>'. All four commands verified with --dry-run.

title: CI: build/deploy jobs skip workspace dependency builds

title: Test runner broken: vitest 4.1.9 imports vite/module-runner, absent in Vite 5.4.21
description: Monorepo-wide: 'pnpm test' (vitest run) fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED because vitest 4.1.9 imports 'vite/module-runner', which Vite 5.4.21 does not export. No package's *.test.ts files can execute under the runner. Impact: blocks the 'all tests pass' acceptance criterion across the repo (auth-react jwt/schedule tests, web client tests, WS2/WS4 suites). Recommend the team lead choose the target versions before anyone bumps.

title: WS3: wire reactive terminal-401 to local session reset
description: A mid-session request whose token refresh fails is a terminal 401. WS1 added setUnauthorizedHandler() in api/client.ts; WS3 owns the session-lifecycle half. Expose auth.expireSession() (local-only performLogout, callApi:false) from the auth-react factory and register it via setUnauthorizedHandler in auth.ts so RequireAuth redirects to /login. Must avoid the loop: never call auth.logout() (which POSTs /auth/logout -> 401 -> re-enters handler).
notes: Implemented: factory exposes auth.expireSession() bridged via factory-scope requestLocalLogout ref, populated by a provider effect; auth.ts registers setUnauthorizedHandler(() => auth.expireSession()). All gates pass: auth-react+web typecheck+build. Local-only (callApi:false) avoids /auth/logout loop.
close_reason: Implemented and verified end-to-end. auth.expireSession() bridge + setUnauthorizedHandler wiring in auth.ts. Browser test (Playwright): terminal 401 on client-side nav redirects to /login, clears both tokens, no loop, no credential leak. Gates: auth-react+web typecheck+build all pass.

apps/web has no error boundary, so any render throw blanks the app
description:
Nothing in apps/web implements componentDidCatch or getDerivedStateFromError. React's default for an uncaught error during render is to unmount the entire tree, so a single bad property access on any page replaces the whole app with an empty white document - no message, no route change, nothing in the UI to indicate what happened.

Found the hard way: /api/dashboard returned {success,data} while DashboardPage expected the payload bare, so dashboard.stats was undefined and .totalSessions threw. The page went blank. DashboardPage has an error branch for exactly this situation - 'Could not load dashboard data' with a Retry button - and it never rendered, because the throw happened during render rather than in the fetch.

The response-shape bug is fixed (commit 13c65f3). This is the reason its symptom was a blank screen instead of a message, and that reason is still there for the next one.
acceptance_criteria: A render error in any routed page shows something the user can act on - at minimum what failed and a way to reload - instead of an empty document. The boundary is exercised by a test that renders a component which throws.
notes: Worth placing per-route rather than only at the root, so one broken page does not take the shell and navigation with it. Also worth logging the caught error, since right now a production render throw leaves no trace at all - it looks identical to a page that simply rendered nothing.

title: Mock API silently fails whenever a base URL is set
description:
apps/web/src/api/mockApi.ts matches endpoints against bare paths - mockAuthApi does `path === AUTH_ENDPOINTS.signup`, i.e. "/auth/signup" - but createMockFetch (line 591) passes through whatever URL the client built:

    if (url.includes("/auth/")) return await mockAuthApi(url, options)

The routing check uses includes() so an absolute URL gets INTO the auth handler, then every equality check inside fails. With VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787 and VITE_USE_MOCK_API=true, signup produces 'Mock endpoint not found: http://localhost:8787/auth/signup' rather than a response.

So the mock works only when the base URL is empty. That is the configuration resolveApiConfig defaults to (config.ts:68 turns the mock on exactly when baseUrl === ""), but VITE_USE_MOCK_API is documented as an explicit override that 'always wins' - and setting it with a base URL present is a reasonable thing to do that fails confusingly. The error names the URL it could not match without saying that the base URL is why.

Hit while switching apps/web to the mock to work around onlooker-7n4.
acceptance_criteria: createMockFetch derives the pathname before dispatching, so the mock works with or without VITE_API_BASE_URL set. A request the mock genuinely does not implement still reports not-found.
notes: One line - parse the pathname (new URL(url, location.origin).pathname, guarding relative inputs) before passing it on. Worth a test that the mock resolves the same endpoint with and without a base URL, since the failure is silent and config-dependent rather than something a normal run surfaces.

title: Settings' white buttons and cream banner are bright blocks on a dark page
description:
feat/web-auth-brand set the app-global background to var(--ground), which is dark by default. Three surfaces still declare their own light fills and now read as bright blocks on a dark page:

  SettingsPage.tsx:408 and :445 - background: "white", 15.9 against the night ground
  SessionExpiryBanner.tsx:45 - #fdf6e3 cream, 14.74 against the night ground

None of these is a contrast failure. Text on each sits on that element's own light fill and passes - the banner's #7a5c00 on #fdf6e3 is 5.80, the buttons' #d93025 on white is 4.77. This is purely how they look.

There is a knock-on that cannot be fixed without fixing the fills. SettingsPage:394's 'Delete account' heading moved to var(--red) during the C1 cleanup, while the delete button at :405-406 kept #d93025 because var(--red) on white is 2.00 at night - a real failure the swap correctly refused. So a heading and button that were one color are now two in both themes, worst at night: light pink #ff9c9c heading above a dark red #d93025 button. The pair can only be reunited by taking the button off white.
acceptance_criteria: Neither SettingsPage's buttons nor SessionExpiryBanner declares a light fill on the dark ground, and the delete-account heading and its button are the same color again in both themes.
notes: The user deliberately deferred these when choosing the C1 fix scope - the decision was to repoint text literals and leave the light fills for their own pass. Doing that pass would also close the heading/button mismatch for free. Related: onlooker-31q, which asks whether apps/web's signed-in pages get the same treatment as the auth surface.
close_reason: Fixed. SettingsPage's two white-filled buttons became ghosts - 'Delete my account' takes --red text and border (7.94/6.48 on the ground, clears 3:1 as a border) rather than a plate, since it only opens the confirmation and filling it would outrank the actual confirm; Cancel takes --ink with an --ink-dim border so it reads as the lesser action beside the filled SubmitButton. SessionExpiryBanner became a filled plate-gold plate with plate-ink text and a plate-ink outline, consistent with FormMessage. The outline is load-bearing per the plate-boundary rule: the gold fill marks the edge at night (12.02 vs the ground) and the outline marks it by day (11.27, where the fill is 1.07). Also closed the knock-on this issue recorded - the delete section's border, heading and trigger button are all var(--red) again, after the earlier cleanup had moved the heading to a token while the button kept a #d93025 literal. Every color in apps/web's pages and components now resolves through a token; the only remaining literal is a #ccc inside a comment.

title: LoginPage has no test coverage at all
description:
apps/web/src/__tests__/auth-form.test.tsx was added on feat/web-auth-brand specifically because the app's only prior test never rendered a component and would have passed with the login form completely broken. It tests components/form.tsx and is genuine for what it covers - six mutations to form.tsx all fail it, and it asserts only roles, labels, ARIA, href, type and disabled, never color, so a restyle cannot break it.

But LoginPage uses none of those components. It is hand-rolled. Six mutations to apps/web/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx were each run against the full suite during the whole-branch review and ALL passed 85/85: dropping htmlFor on both labels, changing the submit button to type="button", making the error banner never render, DELETING the await login(email, password) call entirely, hiding the h1, and changing the <form> to a <div> so submit-on-enter dies.

So the original rationale still holds literally for the page it was written about. Deleting the login call ships green.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation to LoginPage that breaks logging in - removing the login call, breaking the form element, breaking the submit button type - fails the suite.
notes: Related to onlooker-31q, which asks whether LoginPage should be rewired onto the shared components. Doing that would give it this coverage for free rather than duplicating the tests. Worth deciding the rewire first.
close_reason: Fixed. apps/web/src/__tests__/login-page.test.tsx covers what LoginPage itself does: hands the typed credentials to login, navigates to the dashboard on success, honors RequireAuth's returnTo, shows a rejected login's reason without navigating, surfaces a provider-raised error, disables while in flight, and refuses to submit empty fields. Written against the hand-rolled markup FIRST and verified by mutation, not by a green run - deleting the login() call, turning <form> into <div>, changing the submit button's type, removing the error branch, ignoring returnTo, and dropping the htmlFor associations each fail at least one test. All six previously shipped 85/85 green. Then re-verified against the rewired page: same five structural mutations still caught. 85 -> 92 tests.

title: Contrast guard can't see the duplicated theme blocks diverging
description:
packages/brand/tokens.css hand-duplicates 11 declarations between @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) and :root[data-theme="light"], and another 11 between :root and :root[data-theme="dark"]. They are identical today. Nothing asserts that they stay so.

Demonstrated during the feat/web-auth-brand review: setting --teal to #8c1b25, the day RED, in the @media block only, still passes 59/59. Both values independently clear AA against both surfaces, so the per-block loop is satisfied and the divergence is invisible. A user on OS-light with no explicit theme would see 'active / observing' render as red, while a user with data-theme="light" sees teal.

Not covered by onlooker-d14, onlooker-6rr or onlooker-ap1 - those are about which pairings get checked. This is about the same token holding different values in blocks that are supposed to agree.
acceptance_criteria: tokens.test.ts asserts the two light blocks define identical values key-for-key, and likewise the two dark blocks, so a value changed in one place and not its twin fails.
notes: Roughly four lines of test. The duplication itself is arguably the bug - a single source per theme with the selectors sharing it would make divergence impossible rather than merely detectable.
close_reason: Fixed. tokens.test.ts now asserts that :root and :root[data-theme="dark"] define identical values key-for-key, and likewise the two day blocks. Verified by mutation, not by a green run: the exact divergence named in this issue - --teal set to the day red in the media block only - now fails naming the token and both blocks, and removing a token from one twin fails saying which side it is absent from. Plates are excluded from both sides so that a plate leaking into a theme block trips the plate guard that owns that rule rather than this one with a misleading message. 59 -> 61 tests.

title: Login page offers no route to signup or password reset
description:
apps/web/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx renders no links at all. Every sibling auth page has a footer with at least one FormLink; login has none, so a user who has forgotten their password or does not yet have an account has no path forward from the page they land on. /forgot-password and /signup both exist and are routed - they are simply unreachable from the login form.

Found during the feat/web-auth-brand review. That branch could not fix it: it was a skin-only pass, forbidden from adding elements, and LoginPage is hand-rolled rather than built from the shared form components. The reviewer correctly declined to raise it as a finding against the task and flagged it for separate work.
acceptance_criteria: Login offers a visible route to /signup and /forgot-password, styled with the same treatment as the FormLink used on the other auth pages.
notes: Worth deciding at the same time whether LoginPage should be rewired onto the shared AuthCard/TextField/SubmitButton components instead of keeping its parallel inline styles. The brand work brought the two into token-for-token agreement, so the duplication is now the only thing keeping them apart - and it is the reason they drifted in the first place. That rewire was explicitly out of scope for the branding branch because it is a markup restructure on the login path.
close_reason: Fixed as part of rewiring LoginPage onto the shared form components. Its AuthCard footer now carries a FormLink to /forgot-password and one to /signup; both routes already existed in App.tsx and nothing linked to them. The rewire also answered the open question in this issue's notes - LoginPage is no longer a parallel hand-rolled implementation, so the duplication that let the two pages drift is gone, along with ~54 lines, and errors picked up role="alert" which the hand-rolled div lacked.

title: --edge is unfit for its stated job and the guard never checks it
description:
The brand spec designates --edge (#6b64a8, constant in both themes) as the 2px border token - 'never hairlines'. Measured against the two surfaces the package defines, it does not clear the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a boundary:

  vs --ground: 3.04 night, 3.71 day  (night is a 1.3% margin over the threshold)
  vs --panel:  1.79 night, 2.71 day  (fails both)

Worse, the two structures it is actually used in are mirror images and both lean on the 3.04 side with no fallback. A card is a --panel fill on the page --ground; an input is a --ground fill inside that card. In both, the border is the only thing marking the edge, because fill-versus-surrounding is just 1.70 night / 1.37 day either way. If the border does not read, there is no boundary at all.

Nothing catches this. packages/brand/tokens.test.ts checks text tokens only - --ink, --ink-hi, --ink-dim, --gold, --teal, --red - at the 4.5 text threshold. Borders are non-text and want 3.0, and no assertion covers them.

feat/web-auth-brand moves every border in apps/web's auth surface to --ink-dim, which clears both surfaces with margin (8.06/6.56 on ground, 4.74/4.80 on panel). That leaves --edge unused there but still shipped and still named as the border token.
acceptance_criteria: --edge either moves to a value clearing 3.0 against both --ground and --panel in both themes, or is removed and the spec stops calling it the border token. Either way tokens.test.ts gains non-text 3.0 coverage for border tokens against both surfaces, so this cannot regress.
notes: Third instance of the same shape on this project: a token verified for one context and used in another. The others are onlooker-d14 (plates never checked against the surfaces they sit on) and onlooker-6rr (text on surfaces apps derive themselves). Common root is that the guard only covers text-on-the-two-declared-surfaces, and every gap found today lives outside that box.
close_reason: Resolved by reclassifying rather than revaluing. Proved no constant --edge value can clear 3:1 on both surfaces in both themes: the night panel requires luminance >= 0.287 and the day panel <= 0.132, which is unsatisfiable. So --edge cannot be the border token by construction. The spec now documents --ink-dim as the UI boundary token (4.74-8.06 on both surfaces) and --edge as decorative dividers and the grid lattice, exempt from 1.4.11. Its only real requirement, constancy across themes, is now pinned by tokens.test.ts and mutation-verified to fail independently of the twins check. Deliberately did NOT add the 3:1 border assertion the acceptance asked for: --ink-dim is already held to 4.5 on both surfaces, so a 3:1 check could not fail without that failing first - it would read as coverage while providing none. 61 -> 62 tests.

title: Audit apps/website for plate-on-day-surface contrast
description:
The day palette in packages/brand is luminance-flat, so any filled plate is distinguished from its surroundings by hue alone in day mode. Measured against the shipped tokens: plate-teal 1.35 on day ground and 1.01 on day panel, plate-gold 1.07 and 1.46, plate-red 1.61 and 1.18 - all against a 3.0 requirement under WCAG 1.4.11 for identifying UI components. The day theme has almost no luminance range at all: page L~.69, card L~.49, plates L~.50, and the card is only 1.37 against the page. Night mode has real range and is unaffected.

Found while branding apps/web's auth surface on feat/web-auth-brand. That branch fixes it for the auth form by outlining plate-bearing elements in --plate-ink, which gives 7.52 against the day card while the fill continues to carry the boundary at night. apps/website consumes the same tokens and was never checked.

To be fair about severity: these pairs differ sharply in hue and saturation, so they are not invisible to typical color vision. This is a grayscale, color-vision-deficiency and low-vision problem, and a technical 1.4.11 failure. Not urgent, but it is live.
acceptance_criteria: Every filled-plate element in apps/website is enumerated with its measured contrast against the surface it sits on, in both themes. Each either clears 3.0, gains a --plate-ink outline like apps/web's auth form, or is recorded as an accepted hue-only distinction with the reasoning.
notes: Root cause is that the spec verified plate-vs-its-own-ink (7.00-12.02, all fine) and never plate-vs-the-surface-it-sits-on. Same shape as the other guard failures on this project: the value was checked against one thing and used against another. packages/brand/tokens.test.ts still has no assertion for a plate against any surface - only text accents are checked - so this cannot regress-test today.
close_reason: Audited. apps/website has exactly one filled-plate element: the landing page form button (index.astro, background var(--plate-teal) on a var(--panel) form fill). It clears 3.0 in both themes, but via different mechanisms that swap: at night the fill carries the boundary at 4.90 while the adjacent 1px --border-2 separator fails at 2.08; by day the fill is 1.01 and the separator carries it at 3.28, since --border-2 mixes --edge with --ink and shifts per theme. The form's own outer border clears the page ground in both themes (4.00/4.44). No change needed, but the border-left is load-bearing in one theme and looked like trim, so index.astro now says so where someone would remove it. Spec gains a 'plate's own boundary' section with the full plate-vs-surface table and the rule that a plate needs a second boundary mechanism working in the theme where its fill does not - the two in use being a plate-ink outline (apps/web) and a theme-shifting adjacent separator (apps/website). Deliberately added no token-level assertion: whether a plate has a working boundary depends on what it sits beside, which the package cannot see, and asserting plates clear 3:1 against surfaces would fail on all three by design.

title: apps/website routing exists only in the Cloudflare dashboard
description:
apps/website/wrangler.jsonc declares no routes and no custom_domain — just name, assets and observability. The worker is reachable at onlooker.dev because routes were attached in the Cloudflare dashboard, outside this repository. Nothing in version control records how the marketing domain is wired.

That is the same gap that left api-staging.onlooker.dev unreachable for days: a worker deployed, a route that existed only where nobody looked, and no error anywhere. Here it is currently benign because the routes already exist and a redeploy inherits them — but the configuration is undocumented, unreviewable, and one dashboard edit away from being wrong with no diff to show it.

Could not be fixed in the same pass because the live configuration is not readable from an agent session: the Cloudflare worker API returns only name and id, and wrangler is unauthenticated here. Writing route values by guess for the main marketing domain risks taking it down.
design: Read the current configuration first: 'wrangler triggers list' or the Workers > onlooker-community-website > Domains & Routes panel. Match what exists rather than inventing it. Note apps/api uses both styles — custom_domain: true for api-staging, and a plain pattern with zone_name for production — so the repo has no single convention to follow.
acceptance_criteria: apps/website/wrangler.jsonc declares the routes it actually serves, with custom_domain where appropriate, matching what is configured today. Verified by deploying and confirming onlooker.dev still resolves and serves the site — not by the deploy exiting zero.
notes: Found 2026-08-12 while wiring the website deploy into CI. Related: the api-staging incident recorded in the heartbeat design doc.

title: The license-credit test checks source text, not rendered output
description:
apps/website/src/__tests__/credit.test.ts asserts that 'Crusenho Agus Hennihuno' and the CC BY 4.0 URL appear in Layout.astro's raw source. The license condition is that the credit REACHES THE RENDERED PAGE, and a string in a source file does not establish that.

A re-review defeated the test two ways, both applied to a live copy and reverted: wrapping the credit paragraph in an HTML comment, and wrapping it in a false conditional. In both cases the strings remain in the file, the browser renders nothing, and the suite stays 2/2 green.

The test does still catch outright deletion of the paragraph, which was the concrete attack it was written for, so it is not worthless — it is weaker than its own stated goal. ATTRIBUTION.md is explicit that a credit nobody renders does not satisfy CC BY.

This is a defect in the fix that was prescribed, not in its implementation: the reviewer supplied that test code verbatim and the implementer transcribed it faithfully.
design: A build-and-grep check probably belongs in CI rather than a unit test, since building the site per test run is slow. That is a real design choice rather than a quick patch, which is why this is filed instead of squeezed into the branch.
acceptance_criteria: A check that fails when the credit stops rendering, not merely when its text stops existing. Options: build apps/website in CI and grep dist/ for the credit, or render Layout via @astrojs/compiler or a container render and assert against the emitted HTML. Verify by commenting the credit out and confirming the check fails — the two probes above are the acceptance test.
notes: Found by the scoped re-review of the feat/brand-16bit fix wave on 2026-08-11. The credit does render correctly today — confirmed in 18 built HTML files — so the site is compliant now; this is about keeping it that way. Related: onlooker-pbh. When apps/web adopts the icons it will need its own credit surface and the same guard.

title: Publish job cannot tell 'not published' from 'the registry query failed'
description:
The publish-contract job decides whether to publish with:

    published="$(npm view "${name}@${version}" version 2>/dev/null || true)"

Both a genuine 404 and a failed query produce an empty string, and the code treats empty as 'not published yet, go ahead'. So any transient registry problem makes the job attempt a republish.

Observed on 2026-08-10, run 31436357349. Version 2.0.0 was published at 21:56:59.824Z. The next merge's publish job queried the registry at 22:01:22 — four and a half minutes later — and got nothing back, so it tried to publish 2.0.0 again and npm returned E403 'You cannot publish over the previously published versions'. The same query run locally minutes afterward returned 2.0.0 correctly, so the registry was simply still propagating a brand-new package.

Nothing bad reached the registry — npm refused, and publish is atomic. The cost is a red run on a merge where nothing was wrong, and a guard that cannot report which of the two situations it encountered.
design: npm returns non-zero for E404 as well as for real errors, so an exit code alone does not separate them. Capture stdout and stderr together, keep the exit code, and treat 'E404' appearing in the output as the genuine not-found case; anything else non-zero is indeterminate and should stop the job.
acceptance_criteria: The job distinguishes three outcomes: version exists (skip), registry says 404 (publish), query failed for any other reason (fail loudly with an error naming the ambiguity, rather than publishing). Verified by observing each branch — including forcing a query failure, since the whole point is the branch that currently cannot be reached.
notes: Found while verifying the first real publish of @onlooker-community/lesson-contract. Related: onlooker-9eb (parked residuals from the same branch). The E403 is npm working correctly — it is the backstop that kept a bad republish from mattering.
close_reason: Fixed in #20 and verified on the first real run. The publish decision no longer trusts its npm view pre-check: that call is now an explicit fast path documented as non-authoritative, and the publish attempt's own outcome decides. A failure matching 'cannot publish over the previously published versions' exits clean as a no-op; anything else fails. Matches the message rather than the E403 code, since E403 also covers permission denials. Both branches observed: run 31439569436's first attempt correctly reported a real failure as NOT already-published, and the rerun published 2.0.1 successfully. Shipped alongside the OIDC switch, which also carried a provenance attestation.

title: schema.onlooker.dev has never served a schema, and nothing noticed
description:
The onlooker-schemas worker serves its assets from ./public, and public/ contains exactly one file: _headers. The actual schemas live in schemas/ (event.v1.json and payload/), which is not the served directory. Every path on schema.onlooker.dev returns 404 — /, /schemas/, /event.schema.json — and that is correct behavior for an empty asset directory.

The host is deployed, routed and answering, so nothing errors. It just has nothing to serve, and has not since it was set up.

Two claims elsewhere depend on it and are therefore false. The ecosystem's CLAUDE.md states 'Schema drift is caught in CI against the published schemas at schema.onlooker.dev.' Nothing is there to check against, so whatever that check does, it is not comparing against a published schema. The lesson-contract PROVENANCE.json note is accurate but understates it: the host serves no lesson schemas because it serves nothing at all.

This is the same failure class as the api-staging DNS incident and the drift check that only verifies a version pin — infrastructure that looks deployed, errors on nothing, and does nothing. It went unnoticed because no consumer fails when it 404s.
acceptance_criteria: schema.onlooker.dev serves the event schemas at documented, versioned paths, and a request for a known path returns 200 with valid JSON. The ecosystem's CI drift claim is either made true or corrected. Whatever ships is verified by fetching it, not by observing that the deploy succeeded.
notes: Found 2026-08-09 while scoping onlooker-1kg. The host is not covered by the heartbeat, which checks only the four app hosts — that is why this stayed invisible. Consider adding it once it serves something. Source repo: github.com/onlooker-community/schema, wrangler.jsonc routes schema.onlooker.dev/* with zone_name (no custom_domain), assets.directory = ./public.
close_reason: INVALID — my error. schema.onlooker.dev works: /schemas/event.v1.json and /schemas/payload/session.json both return 200 with valid JSON, and the event schema's $id is that URL. public/ holds only _headers in git because .gitignore line 3 is 'public/schemas/' — the schemas are build output written by scripts/prepare-static-assets.js during deploy-schemas.yml. I mistook a gitignored build directory for the served content and tested wrong filenames (event.schema.json rather than event.v1.json). The ecosystem's CLAUDE.md claim that CI checks drift against schema.onlooker.dev is true.

title: Lesson schemas are generated but never published, so the ecosystem's drift check cannot check drift
description:
packages/lesson-contract generates lesson.schema.json and counter-observation.schema.json, but nothing publishes them. schema.onlooker.dev 404s on every lesson path — that host serves the ecosystem's event schemas, not ours.

The ecosystem repo shipped its lesson transform on 2026-08-09 (PR #132) and had to vendor copies into plugins/librarian/schema/*.subschema.json, because its hooks are bash and cannot import our zod source. Its guard, scripts/lint/check-lesson-schema-drift.mjs, says so in its own header: it 'cannot compare against the upstream schema until schema.onlooker.dev publishes lesson schemas.' All it actually verifies is that PROVENANCE.json still pins schema_version 2 and that the vendored files parse.

So the failure is silent and one-directional. If we bump the contract to schema_version 3, their copies stay at 2, their drift check stays green, and their transform keeps emitting lessons against a contract that no longer exists. The API's ingest endpoint would reject them — which is the right backstop, but it turns a contract change here into a mystery outage there.

Note this is exactly the rot the lesson contract was designed to prevent, reappearing one level up: the thing that goes stale is the schema rather than a lesson.
design: Open: whether to serve from the existing onlooker-schemas worker behind a versioned path, publish the package to npm so consumers pin a version, or both. The ecosystem's own precedent is a URL, and its hooks are bash with no node_modules, which argues for the URL. Do not decide this without checking what the ecosystem side actually wants to consume.
acceptance_criteria: A consumer in another repo can fetch the current lesson schema over the network and compare it against a vendored copy, and ecosystem's check-lesson-schema-drift.mjs can be pointed at it. Bumping schema_version in packages/lesson-contract makes that check fail rather than silently pass. Publishing must be automatic on release — a manual upload step reintroduces the same drift one layer up.
notes: Found 2026-08-09 while checking whether the AGENTS.md mirror had gone stale after ecosystem PR #132 merged. Related: onlooker-97e (the promotion pipeline handoff, closed).
close_reason: Implemented on feat/publish-lesson-contract. packages/lesson-contract publishes as @onlooker-community/lesson-contract@2.0.0 with schema/ in the tarball, so the ecosystem's check-lesson-schema-drift.mjs can import and compare instead of only verifying a provenance pin. Two guards: the pre-existing freshness check (fixed to see untracked files) and a new version-bump guard that also rejects a version decrease. Publishing is gated on NPM_TOKEN, which does not exist yet.

title: Record the dashboard design and correct the heartbeat's cadence claims
description: Two related doc gaps left by the heartbeat work. (1) The spec asserts a five-minute cadence and derives numbers from it, but GitHub delivers the '*/5' cron at ~31 min — measured across three consecutive runs on 2026-08-09. Three statements are now false or misleading: 'six requests every five minutes', 'roughly 1,440 rows a day' (the argument against a login-based heartbeat, off by ~30x), and 'the minimum GitHub Actions supports' (true of cron syntax, misleading about delivery). (2) The Cloudflare dashboard design exists only in a chat transcript: four dashboards, their charts, and — critically — the filter identifiers. Those identifiers are invisible from the dashboard UI and a wrong one renders a plausible chart rather than an error, so losing them is worse than losing the chart list.
acceptance_criteria: Spec and plan no longer assert a cadence contradicted by measurement, and the rows-per-day argument is restated with a number that holds at the real rate. A dashboard doc exists covering all four dashboards, each chart in prose, and the exact filters: hostnames, the four deployed script names with their env suffixes, both D1 names and UUIDs, and the three unrelated account workers that must be excluded. Corrected volume figures appear once, in the doc, not scattered.
notes: Do not simply change the cron to '*/30'. It would make the config match observed behavior but produces no additional runs, and the ~31 min figure comes from a 1.5 h sample that may loosen. Document the gap between requested and delivered instead. Source: onlooker-2ho notes.
close_reason: Shipped in #17: cadence corrected against measurement, docs/observability-dashboards.md records all four dashboards and the filter identifiers.

title: Test that revoking a refresh token does not delete other sessions
description: Found by the final whole-branch review of the database source-of-truth work. If revokeRefreshToken lost its where clause it would delete EVERY session, and all 13 characterization tests would still pass - nothing asserts that another user's sessions survive a revoke. The where clause IS present; the safety net is just thinner than it looks on the highest-risk line in the auth query layer. Add a test that stores sessions for two users, revokes one, and asserts the other survives.
close_reason: Test added in apps/api/src/db/queries.test.ts. Verified non-vacuous by mutation rather than assumed: stripping the where clause from revokeRefreshToken makes exactly this test fail while the other 13 still pass, which is precisely the blind spot the final review identified.

title: applies_to.versions keys are not constrained to stack entries
description: ZAppliesTo documents versions as 'keyed by stack entry' but nothing enforces it: {stack:['vite'], scope:{kind:'versioned', versions:{nothing:'<6'}}} parses clean. Found by the final whole-branch review of lesson contract v2. Depending on how retrieval treats an unmatched key, the lesson either never matches or the constraint is skipped - and the skip case is the same never-expires failure class that the applies_to.scope union exists to close. Fix is a .check() on ZAppliesTo asserting Object.keys(versions) is a subset of stack. Not expressible in JSON Schema (it is a cross-field rule), so runtime-only is correct here; document it alongside the existing 'agreed <= judges' ingest rule.
design: Runtime .check() on ZAppliesTo, not on ZVersions, since it needs both fields. Refinements are dropped by z.toJSONSchema, so the published artifact cannot carry this - it belongs with the other cross-field rules enforced at apps/api ingest. Decide whether plugins should also self-check before emitting.
close_reason: Resolved as far as the contract can resolve it, following the ZConsensus precedent. A .check() was rejected: it would make packages/lesson-contract reject values the published JSON Schema accepts, and the shell-based plugins validate against that artifact and cannot import the package - an invisible rule would fail them with no way to have known. Instead ZAppliesTo now carries a .describe() stating that every scope.versions key must name a stack entry and that the rule is enforced at ingest, which reaches the artifact where plugin authors can see it. A structural fix (moving ranges onto stack entries) was considered and rejected as not worth a schema_version 3 once it turned out not to remove the existing .check()/.meta() pair. The enforcement itself is now listed in the promotion pipeline spec's cross-field ingest rules table alongside 'agreed <= judges', for whoever builds the sync endpoint.

title: Handoff: promotion pipeline in the plugin repo (transform, rubric, pool)
description: Sections 2-3 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-promotion-pipeline-design.md, which land in the onlooker-community plugin repo rather than here. Librarian gains a fifth stage (Haiku lesson transform) reusing its existing last_scan.json watermark; tribunal gains a lesson-promotion rubric with max_iterations 1. Human confirms candidates and intended visibility before any Opus tokens are spent. Gating is visibility-scoped: private no jury, org rubric, public rubric plus the already-shipped tribunal-judge-security as the disclosure lens. State under ~/.onlooker/librarian/<key>/lessons/{approved,declined.jsonl}. Acceptance test is the real archivist artifact 01KZ45MKAM734ZS7JK24D2DK0R, which must transform to kind=versioned {vite:<6, vitest:>=4} and not match a vite 8 session.
close_reason: Tracking moved to the ecosystem repo, where the implementation lands. Superseded by ecosystem-4z8 (epic) with children ecosystem-4z8.1 through 4z8.5: Haiku lesson transform, human confirmation, tribunal lesson-promotion rubric, approved pool and declined ledger, and the author_key derivation decision. Design content ported in full; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-promotion-pipeline-design.md in this repo remains the authoritative spec.

title: Implement lesson contract v2: applies_to.scope union and wider author_key
description: Subsystem 2's in-repo half. Apply Section 1 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-promotion-pipeline-design.md to packages/lesson-contract: replace applies_to.versions with the applies_to.scope discriminated union, widen ZAuthorKey to 32 hex, bump schema_version to 2, regenerate both JSON Schema artifacts. Resolves onlooker-7jn and onlooker-5oz. Two migration chores: every fixture using a 12-hex author_key needs widening, and emit-json-schema.mjs reads from ../dist/index.js so the package must be built before regenerating or the committed schema goes stale silently.
acceptance_criteria: versioned branch rejects {} at runtime AND emits minProperties:1 (asserted separately); version_independent requires non-empty justification; unknown kind rejected; version-range pattern still asserted inside scope.oneOf; author_key 32 hex and project_key still 12; schema_version literal 2; committed-schema drift guard passes
close_reason: Lesson contract v2 shipped on feat/lesson-contract-v2. applies_to.scope discriminated union makes an unexpiring lesson unrepresentable (empty map, vacuous >=0 range, and unjustified version_independent all rejected); author_key widened to 128 bits; schema_version 2 on both schemas. 49/49 tests, zero schema drift.

title: applies_to.versions={} conflates version-independent with inference failure
description: ZAppliesTo accepts an empty versions map. That makes 'this lesson genuinely does not depend on a version' indistinguishable from 'the Haiku transform failed to infer versions', and the spec itself notes applies_to cannot be reliably inferred from an artifact. A lesson with versions={} never expires structurally, which is the one guarantee the whole contract rests on - so an inference failure silently produces an immortal lesson. Found by the final whole-branch review of the lesson contract. Disposition: not a contract bug, since the schema cannot tell the two cases apart. The transform (subsystem 2, promotion pipeline) must either always emit at least one version constraint or explicitly mark a lesson version-independent. Decide there, then reflect it in the spec.
design: RESOLVED 2026-08-08 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-promotion-pipeline-design.md Section 1. Chose option (a) hardened: applies_to.versions is replaced by applies_to.scope, a discriminated union on kind. Branch 'versioned' requires a non-empty versions map; branch 'version_independent' requires a written justification that the tribunal scores via the scope_accuracy criterion. Inference failure can no longer produce a valid lesson - it fails schema validation. Non-emptiness is enforced twice because neither mechanism alone suffices: .check() covers runtime (zod refinements are dropped by z.toJSONSchema) and .meta({minProperties:1}) covers the emitted artifact (.meta does NOT affect runtime validation). Verified in zod 4.4.3. Record kept over array-of-pairs so keys stay unique by construction. Costs schema_version 2.
close_reason: Lesson contract v2 shipped on feat/lesson-contract-v2. applies_to.scope discriminated union makes an unexpiring lesson unrepresentable (empty map, vacuous >=0 range, and unjustified version_independent all rejected); author_key widened to 128 bits; schema_version 2 on both schemas. 49/49 tests, zero schema drift.

title: apps/web ignores the brand established in apps/website
description: The product UI shares no visual language with the marketing site. apps/website/src/styles/globals.css defines a real identity - 258 lines with tokens: --bg #080c10, --accent #00d4aa, --sans Syne, --mono DM Mono, dark terminal aesthetic. apps/web uses NONE of it: zero CSS files, zero className usage, no styling dependency, no font declaration at all (so browser default serif), and 71 inline style={{}} objects across 9 pages. Its palette is default framework colors - #007bff (bootstrap blue), #d93025/#188038 (material red/green), #666/#ccc grays. The brand accent #00d4aa appears nowhere in the product. Work: decide the styling mechanism (plain CSS + custom properties reusing the website tokens, vs a framework), extract the shared tokens somewhere both apps can consume, and restyle the 9 auth/dashboard pages. Landing page already proves the aesthetic works, so this is adoption rather than design from scratch.
design: Prefer lifting the existing globals.css tokens into a shared package over inventing a new system - the visual decisions are already made and shipped on the marketing site. Subsystem 6 in the shared lesson contract spec.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/brand-16bit. packages/brand now holds the color tokens, fonts and 80 icons with their licenses, and apps/website consumes it — so the two no longer drift by default. A contrast test parses tokens.css and asserts the palette rules, including the day palette that actually renders. apps/web adoption is a separate plan: it has no styling layer at all, 71 inline style props and no CSS. Residual: onlooker-8m1 (the license-credit guard checks source text rather than rendered output).

title: packages/db drizzle schema and apps/api raw SQL have drifted apart
description: apps/api does not depend on @onlooker/db - it hand-writes SQL in src/db/queries.ts against a 3-table schema (users, sessions with token_hash, verification_tokens) defined in apps/api/migrations/0001_init.sql. packages/db/src/schema.ts defines a different 7-table drizzle schema (adds password_reset_tokens, email_change_tokens, machine_tokens, audit_logs) whose sessions table uses 'token' not 'token_hash'. packages/db has tests that pass against its own schema, so both look healthy in isolation while describing incompatible databases. PR #7 pinned migrations_dir to apps/api/migrations so deploys cannot pick the wrong one, but the underlying divergence remains: features written against packages/db will not work, and the extra 4 tables exist nowhere real. Decide on one source of truth.
close_reason: Rebuild executed 2026-08-09. Both D1 databases dropped and rebuilt from the drizzle baseline; d1_migrations cleared so the false ledger is discarded rather than built upon. Verified by direct query, not by log: production users.email_verified is now text (was BOOLEAN), first_name/last_name gone, sessions.token_hash carries its UNIQUE index and the FK cascades, audit_logs and its five undeclared indexes removed, 9 indexes matching the generated migration, and d1_migrations records exactly 0000_kind_starjammers.sql. The CI schema verifier ran between migrate and deploy in both environments, so neither worker shipped against an unverified schema. Real signup/login round-trips pass on both api-staging and api, and the persisted row shows email_verified as a genuine null with a 64-char token hash. test@onlooker.dev was dropped deliberately - it was disposable test data with all name fields null, which also removed the boolean-to-timestamp remapping entirely.

title: Design: Shared Lesson contract for cross-machine Playbooks
description: Design spec for the atom of Shared Playbooks. Decisions locked in brainstorming: (1) hosted app exists for cross-person lesson sharing; (2) lessons are the unit, Playbooks are saved-query views; (3) retrieval is tiered — cheap always-on plus deep on demand (Waypoint); (4) promotion gated by tribunal-style N-agent consensus; (5) private/org/public visibility in one pool from the start; (6) contract shape B — claim + evidence + applicability, with a reserved status field so lifecycle is additive. Driving constraint: a real archivist artifact in this repo (vitest/vite mismatch) is now false and would mislead if shared, so staleness must be structural rather than a later phase. Scope is the contract only; retrieval engine, sync API, web app, and visual system are separate sub-projects.
design: Shape B: normative claim + evidence receipts + applicability conditions. Version-scoped applicability lets lessons expire by construction rather than by review.
notes: Spec COMPLETE 2026-08-07 - all five sections approved. Section 3: author_key = HMAC(user_secret, scope) so org and public identities are unlinkable; visibility moves up only, downward is retraction; org keeps custody when a member leaves; public needs a safety/disclosure lens distinct from correctness because correctness rots and harm does not. Section 4: expiry is NOT a status (applies_to just stops matching, no sweep job); contradiction is a signal that triggers tribunal re-judgment, never an automatic verdict; supersession detected by existing Jaccard step, confirmed by consensus; nothing is ever deleted. Section 5: plugins are shell-based in a SEPARATE repo, so the producing side cannot import zod - zod is source of truth, z.toJSONSchema emits the published artifact, apps/api sync endpoint is the enforcement boundary; server accepts schema_version N and N-1 because the two sides cannot upgrade atomically; dedicated packages/lesson-contract chosen over @onlooker/types to avoid inheriting node-html-parser. Next step is writing-plans, not implementation. Known open number: counter-observation threshold in Section 4.
close_reason: Design complete and shipped. All five spec sections approved (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-shared-lesson-contract-design.md); scope was the contract only, and packages/lesson-contract shipped it as v1 (PR #9) then v2 (PR #10). Downstream subsystems have their own beads: onlooker-97e (promotion pipeline), onlooker-jpn (applies_to keys).

title: Create Deployment Status step fails on every production deploy
description: The final step of deploy-production calls github.rest.repos.createDeploymentStatus with deployment_id: context.payload.deployment.id. The workflow triggers on push, and push event payloads have no 'deployment' key — that field only exists on deployment/deployment_status events. Result: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id'), so the job reports failure even though both wrangler deploys succeeded (onlooker-api-production 725e1537, onlooker-web-production 7e9db277). Cosmetic but persistent: it will fail on every deploy and masks whether a real deploy problem occurred. The step is redundant anyway — GitHub already records deployments via the job's environment: block.

title: Add hook-layer test for useAuthenticatedFetch terminal-401 surfacing
description: Companion to onlooker-rno (WS1, transport+mock layer). Clean boundary, zero overlap: onlooker-rno proves the transport EMITS exactly one terminal signal (single /auth/refresh coalesce, single onUnauthorized on refresh-of-refresh failure, no retry loop) by testing client.ts + mockApi.ts directly with no React. THIS bead proves the HOOK faithfully SURFACES that one signal. Covers apps/web/src/hooks/useAuthenticatedFetch.ts. Approach: mount the hook (React test renderer / @testing-library/react-hooks equivalent) and mock the apiClient.request boundary so the transport is stubbed — the hook must not add retry/refresh of its own (that lives in the transport). Blocked on the web vitest runner (onlooker-sju).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Happy path: hook goes loading:true -> data set, loading:false, error:null; apiClient.request called exactly once. 2) Terminal 401: request rejects once with AuthApiError(401,'Session expired'); hook exposes error==='Session expired' exactly once, loading:false, data:null, and request is called EXACTLY ONCE (no hook-level retry — the single terminal signal is surfaced, not duplicated or swallowed). 3) Non-401 error (e.g. 500 after transport retries exhausted): surfaced as error string once; hook does NOT call auth.refresh() or clear session (that is transport/WS3's concern, not the hook's). 4) refetch(): re-issues the request, clears prior error, returns to loading:true. 5) skip:true issues no request (loading:false, no call). 6) Unmount mid-flight: no state update after unmount (active-flag guard; no act/setState-after-unmount warning). Suite green under the fixed runner.
notes: Sibling to onlooker-rno per WS1 boundary agreement: rno=transport emits one signal, this=hook surfaces one signal. WS4 owns these acceptance criteria (own hook surface). File now, runs when onlooker-sju (runner fix) lands.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add apps/web tests for JWT/exp mock + refresh transport (blocked on runner)
description: WS1 (Real API Integration) added behavior to apps/web that currently has no automated coverage because the web vitest runner is broken (onlooker-sju). Once the runner works, cover: (1) mock issues JWT-shaped access/refresh tokens with real exp; getTokenExpiration parses exp from the payload. (2) exp enforcement: expired access -> 401 on /auth/me; expired refresh -> 401 on /auth/refresh. (3) hybrid validation: in-session owner-map is authoritative (rotation/logout/email-rename); stateless decodeJwtPayload+exp fallback validates a still-valid token after the owner map is cold (reload safety). (4) revocation: invalidateSessions / logout add tokens to REVOKED_TOKENS and subsequent use 401s. (5) transport single-flight refresh: one 401 storm coalesces into a single /auth/refresh, then replays; refresh-of-refresh failure surfaces the terminal 401 and fires onUnauthorized exactly once (no retry loop). Files: apps/web/src/api/mockApi.ts, apps/web/src/api/client.ts.
acceptance_criteria: Vitest suite in apps/web covering exp enforcement, hybrid/reload validation, revocation, and single-flight refresh+terminal-401; green under the fixed runner.

title: WS1: mock issues exp-bearing JWTs + stateless validation (reload-safe, activates refresh/expiry)

Fix in apps/web/src/api/mockApi.ts: issueTokens mints real JWTs with exp (access short, refresh long); token->email resolution becomes hybrid — in-memory Maps stay authoritative in-session (preserves rotation/logout/WS2 email-rename), falling back to stateless decodeJwtPayload+exp check when Maps are cold (post-reload) so a seeded session survives reload. Enforce exp so reactive refresh-on-401 fires. Revoke superseded tokens on rotation/logout. No signature changes to emailFromAuthHeader/requireAuth so WS2/WS4 handlers are unaffected.

Verified: encode<->decode round-trip against auth-react decoder (11/11 checks incl UTF-8, exp, opaque->null); typecheck/lint/build green. Browser demo (reload persistence + expiry warning firing) handed to WS3 to confirm.

apps/web declares no color-scheme, so autofill repaints the login fields
description:
Nothing in the repo declares color-scheme. With the dark --ground fill the auth inputs now carry, Chrome treats the page as light and paints autofilled fields its light-blue autofill background - which every returning user hits on the login form, on the two fields they always autofill.

Same root cause, latent: TextField exposes a placeholder prop (form.tsx:133,145,164) but styles no ::placeholder. No page passes a placeholder today, so nothing renders wrong yet, but the UA default is a dark gray that would sit on a dark fill.

Found during the feat/web-auth-brand whole-branch review. One line in packages/brand/tokens.css - color-scheme: dark light on :root, with the per-theme blocks setting it explicitly - covers both.
acceptance_criteria: Autofilled login fields render with the brand's own colors in both themes, and a placeholder passed to TextField is legible on the input's fill.
notes: Worth checking in a real browser rather than by computation - autofill styling is UA-specific and not something contrast math can confirm.

title: --shadow and --mark are checked against nothing
description:
Two brand tokens have no contrast coverage at all, both demonstrated during the feat/web-auth-brand review by mutating them to useless values and watching the suite stay green at 59/59.

--shadow carries the hard offset shadow that is the signature of the 16-bit treatment. It measures 1.16 against the night ground and 1.97 against the night panel; day is 1.99 and 1.45. Setting --shadow to #221f38, making the shadow vanish entirely, passes. Decorative shadows are not bound by WCAG 1.4.11, so this is not a conformance failure - but the numbers say the effect barely renders in the default theme, and nobody has looked at it in a browser.

--mark is #db3a3a, kept for non-text use. tokens.test.ts only enforces that #db3a3a is used AS --mark; nothing checks that --mark is visible on anything. It is 2.08 against the night panel, below the 3:1 non-text floor. Setting it to #464074, making it invisible against the panel, passes.
acceptance_criteria: --mark clears 3.0 against both surfaces in both themes, or is documented as valid only on specific surfaces with the guard enforcing that. --shadow gets a deliberate decision recorded - either a floor it must clear, or a note that it is decorative and exempt - after someone has actually looked at it rendered.
notes: --shadow is the strongest 'only eyes can settle it' item on the brand work. 1.16 is either the subtle depth intended or invisible, and contrast math cannot tell you which.

title: apps/website derives a third surface the brand tokens never check
description:
packages/brand defines two surfaces, --ground and --panel, and its contrast test checks every text token against both. apps/website derives a third: globals.css:18 sets --bg-3 to color-mix(in srgb, var(--panel) 82%, var(--ink)), which resolves to #605b8b at night and #9e9ebe by day. Nothing verifies text against it.

--text-3 (aliased to --ink-dim) lands on it at pages/plugins/[slug].astro:478 - td code.dim inside a tbody tr:hover row at :468. Measured 3.16 night / 3.56 day, under the 4.5 that size of text needs. --red, --teal and --ink itself (4.42 night) also fail against --bg-3.

Found during the feat/web-auth-brand review. Note the direction of travel: the token fix on that branch IMPROVED every one of these - night ink-dim went 2.23 to 3.16, day 2.68 to 3.56, night red 2.75 to 3.12 - so this is a smaller residual of a bug that was worse before, not a regression.

apps/web has no derived surfaces, so the package's two-surface model is complete for that app.
acceptance_criteria: Either --bg-3 moves far enough from the text tokens that everything landing on it clears AA in both themes, or the surface is dropped in favor of --panel. Whichever way it goes, the contrast guard covers it, so a derived surface cannot go unchecked again.
notes: The general shape is that packages/brand guarantees contrast for the surfaces IT defines, and an app can derive a new one with color-mix and silently leave that guarantee behind. Worth deciding whether derived surfaces are allowed at all. Related: onlooker-d14, which is the same class of gap for plates rather than text.

title: release.yml depends on actions/create-release, which is archived
description:
release.yml cuts a GitHub Release with actions/create-release@v1. That repository is archived — confirmed via the API — so it receives no fixes, security or otherwise. This is distinct from the Node 20 migration handled in onlooker-0n7: the problem is abandonment, not runtime.

Two things keep it from being urgent. release.yml is workflow_dispatch only, so it never runs on a merge, and the action still works today. But an archived dependency in a release path is the kind of thing that breaks at the worst moment and has no upstream to fix it.

Replacing it is a decision rather than a version bump. Options are softprops/action-gh-release, which is the widely used third-party successor, or 'gh release create' in a run step, which adds no dependency at all and matches how this repo already leans on gh elsewhere.

Worth revisiting the tagging scheme in the same pass: it tags v${{ github.run_number }}, so tags track how many times the workflow has run rather than anything about the software. That is unrelated to the archived action but lives in the same nine lines.
acceptance_criteria: release.yml no longer depends on an archived action. Because the workflow is workflow_dispatch only, it cannot be verified by merging — trigger it manually against a non-production target and confirm a release is actually created, rather than trusting a green run.
notes: Split out of onlooker-0n7 on 2026-08-10, which covered only the node20 runtime bumps. The tag-by-run-number question is noted rather than decided.

title: Revisit author_key width once HMAC derivation is implemented
description: The lesson contract pins author_key to 12 lowercase hex characters, matching ZProjectKey. That is a truncated HMAC: 48 bits, so collision resistance is weak at scale (birthday bound around 16M identities per scope) even though unlinkability is unaffected by truncation. Section 3 of the spec defines author_key = HMAC(user_secret, scope). When subsystem 2 actually derives these keys, confirm 12 hex is wide enough for the expected identity count per scope, or widen the contract and bump schema_version. Raised while applying final-review fixes; the 12-hex choice was taken deliberately for consistency with project_key and because existing fixtures use it.
design: RESOLVED 2026-08-08 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-promotion-pipeline-design.md Section 1. ZAuthorKey widens from 12 to 32 lowercase hex (48 -> 128 bits). ZProjectKey stays at 12: it is a local-only opaque label with no security role, and the two were only ever coupled by convention. Rationale: Section 3 of the contract spec gives author_key two collision-sensitive jobs, org revocation and public blocking, where a collision blocks an innocent author alongside a bad actor. Rides along free on the schema_version 2 bump that onlooker-7jn already forces.
close_reason: Lesson contract v2 shipped on feat/lesson-contract-v2. applies_to.scope discriminated union makes an unexpiring lesson unrepresentable (empty map, vacuous >=0 range, and unjustified version_independent all rejected); author_key widened to 128 bits; schema_version 2 on both schemas. 49/49 tests, zero schema drift.
